questions.stem:
Newman projections P, Q, R and S are shown below (For each projection, one carbon carries the groups at top, lower-left and lower-right; the other carbon carries the groups at upper-left, upper-right and bottom.):
P — top: CH₃; upper-right: CH₃; lower-right: C₂H₅; bottom: CH₃; lower-left: H₃C; upper-left: HO
Q — top: C(CH₃)₂OH (drawn as H₃C–C(OH)–CH₃); upper-right: H; lower-right: C₂H₅; bottom: CH₃; lower-left: H; upper-left: H
R — top: CH₃; upper-right: H; lower-right: CH₃; bottom: C₂H₅; lower-left: HO; upper-left: C₂H₅
S — top: CH₃; upper-right: CH(CH₃)₂; lower-right: H; bottom: OH; lower-left: H; upper-left: C₂H₅
Which one of the following options represents identical molecules?
questions.solution: Read the three groups on each carbon and join the two carbons. P is (CH₃)₂C(OH)–C(CH₃)₂C₂H₅, i.e. 2,3,3-trimethylpentan-2-ol. Q is (CH₃)₂C(OH)–CH(C₂H₅)–CH₂CH₃ and R is (CH₃)₂C(OH)–CH(C₂H₅)₂. These are the same compound, 3-ethyl-2-methylpentan-2-ol. S is CH₃CH₂–C(OH)(C₂H₅)CH(CH₃)₂, i.e. 3-ethyl-2-methylpentan-3-ol. None of them has a stereocentre, so Q and R are identical.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Which one of the following structures has the IUPAC name 3-ethynyl-2-hydroxy-4-methylhex-3-en-5-ynoic acid?
questions.solution: Build the name: C1 is COOH and C2 carries OH. C3=C4 is the double bond, with an ethynyl on C3 and a methyl on C4. C5≡C6 is the terminal triple bond in the main chain. So the compound is HOOC–CH(OH)–C(C≡CH)=C(CH₃)–C≡CH, which is D. A and C have both ethynyls on C4, and B has an ethyl in place of the methyl.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
The Fischer projection of D-erythrose is shown below.
D-Erythrose and its isomers are listed as P, Q, R, and S in Column-I. Choose the correct relationship of P, Q, R, and S with D-erythrose from Column II.
Column-I: P, Q, R, S (structures shown)
Column-II: 1. Diastereomer; 2. Identical; 3. Enantiomer
questions.solution: D-Erythrose is (2R,3R). Assign CIP descriptors to each wedge–dash drawing: P is (2R,3R), Q is (2S,3R), R is (2R,3S) and S is (2S,3S). Matching both centres means identical (P). Inverting both means the enantiomer (S, L-erythrose). Inverting only one means a diastereomer (Q and R, the threoses). So P→2, Q→1, R→1, S→3.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: With respect to the compounds I-V, choose the correct statement(s).

options.text: The acidity of compound I is due to delocalization in the conjugate base.
The conjugate base of compound IV is aromatic.
Compound II becomes more acidic, when it has a -NO₂ substituent.
The acidity of compounds follows the order I > IV > V > II > III.

questions.solution: Losing H⁺ from Ph₃CH gives a trityl anion whose charge spreads over three rings (A true). The cyclopentadienyl anion has 6π electrons in a planar ring, so it is aromatic (B true). An NO₂ group pulls electron density away and stabilises the aryl anion, so nitrobenzene's ring C–H is more acidic than benzene's (C true). The approximate pKa values are cyclopentadiene ≈ 16, ethyne ≈ 25, Ph₃CH ≈ 31, benzene ≈ 43 and methane ≈ 50. The order is therefore IV > V > I > II > III, so D is false.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
In the reaction scheme shown below, Q, R, and S are the major products.
P —succinic anhydride, AlCl₃→ Q —(i) Zn-Hg/HCl (ii) H₃PO₄→ R —(i) CH₃MgBr (ii) H₃O⁺ (iii) H₂SO₄/Δ→ S
The correct structure of
questions.solution: P has three free ring positions. The one between the t-Bu and the gem-dimethyl carbon is blocked, and the one next to t-Bu is crowded. Friedel–Crafts acylation with succinic anhydride therefore goes to the ring CH next to the ring CH₂, giving the keto acid Q (B). Clemmensen reduction turns the C=O into CH₂. H₃PO₄ then closes a six-membered ring by intramolecular acylation at the only free ortho position, next to the t-Bu carbon. So R's ketone sits beside the t-Bu-bearing carbon, not where C draws it. CH₃MgBr gives a tertiary alcohol, and acid dehydration gives the methyl-substituted alkene conjugated with the ring. That is S as drawn in D; A puts the methyl on the wrong carbon.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
In the following reaction, compound Q is obtained from compound P via an ionic intermediate.
P —conc. H₂SO₄→ Q (A colored compound)
What is the degree of unsaturation of Q?
questions.solution: In conc. H₂SO₄ the crowded ester loses methanol and forms an acylium ion, ArC≡O⁺. This ion attacks an ortho phenyl ring (intramolecular Friedel–Crafts acylation). The product Q is 1,3-diphenylfluoren-9-one, which is yellow. Q is C₂₅H₁₆O: DoU = (2×25 + 2 − 16)/2 = 18. Check: four benzene rings (16) + the five-membered ring (1) + C=O (1) = 18.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
